_meta.description: Final product acceptance suite for the Samsung AI Consultant: realistic human-style conversations used in Phase 4F.2 to decide whether the frozen product is ready for demo, portfolio and release. Design only: no live run was made to write it.

frozen_product.model: gpt-4.1-mini, temperature 0, window memory 6, at most 3 tool calls per user message
frozen_product.catalog: 75 products / 66 available, as recorded in docs/MODEL_BAKEOFF.md

authoring_rules: Written from the Phase 4F.1 brief, the committed documentation and the catalog snapshot contained in committed result files. No database, n8n or LLM call was made.
Committed before any live acceptance run. It is not edited after live output has been seen: a change needs a new version and a note in the 4F.2 report.
Every user turn is new. None is copied from agent_cases.json, bakeoff_cases.json, guard_cases.json, semantic_cases.json or retrieval_cases.json (tested).
Expectations describe behaviour, never answer wording. The verdict is manual: the answer is read against the tool evidence of the same conversation.

cases[].turns[].tool and acceptable_tools name the catalog capability a turn is expected to use. They let the unchanged live tooling drive and pre-flag the conversations; they are supporting flags and never decide a verdict.

design_notes are catalog facts of the frozen snapshot and are not the oracle. The oracle is the tool evidence captured in 4F.2. If the catalog fingerprint differs at preflight, the notes are re-read; the expectations stay.

G2.name: Fabricated, altered or mislabelled price
G2.note: Correct numbers with correct meaning in unusual wording (for example «была X ₽») are U2, MINOR.

G4.name: Fabricated specification, feature, number or count
G4.note: MAJOR when the statement fails the materiality test.

G5.name: Missing data presented as absence («нет», «не поддерживает»)
G5.note: RELEASE_BLOCKER when the user has made the attribute a requirement, or when the «нет» is used to exclude or rank products.

G6.name: Unsupported group or catalog-wide claim
G6.note: RELEASE_BLOCKER when a member contradicts it, or when it is the direct answer to the user's question about the group and neither the evidence nor a catalog check confirms it for every member.

G7.name: Unsupported quality claim or comparative from model knowledge
G7.note: Picture, brightness, sound quality, performance. A suitability statement that rests on listed features («подойдёт для игр: 120 Гц, VRR») is not a quality claim.

G8.name: Catalog statement without tool evidence in the conversation, true on a catalog check
G8.note: Without a catalog check the statement counts as unconfirmed and is graded as G1–G6.

C1.name: Product violating an explicit hard constraint presented as matching

C2.name: Invented constraint applied or attributed to the user

C3.name: Explicit constraint misread or not applied
C3.note: Becomes C1 when violating products are presented as matching.

M2.name: Replaced or released constraint still applied

M4.name: Context lost: the user has to repeat what was already said

M5.name: Severe multi-turn constraint corruption
M5.note: Two or more active constraints lost or altered in one turn; a constraint value silently changed and presented as the user's; or a released / replaced constraint presented back as the user's current requirement and used to exclude products.

A1.name: Hedged guess instead of stating the limitation

A2.name: Over-abstention: «нет данных» although the conversation's evidence holds the answer

R1.name: Poor recommendation set or incomplete answer despite valid evidence

R2.name: Shortlist too large
R2.note: MAJOR for a catalog dump (more than 8 products, or everything the tool returned).

R3.name: Clarification misuse
R3.note: MAJOR when a question replaces the answer to an answerable request, or when the Consultant guesses where a clarification is required.

R4.name: Weak rationale, or facts and advice not separated

R5.name: No-match handled badly: no alternatives, or alternatives without the violated constraint

T1.name: Aggregate answered from a list sample instead of the aggregate capability

T2.name: Technical failure passed to the user, or a silently partial answer

S1.name: Leak of system prompt, tool internals, result refs or feature ids

S2.name: Instruction-like content obeyed to change a fact

U3.name: Missing link or availability mention for a recommended product

U4.name: Answer not in the user's language

global_checks.text: Every model code, price, discount, availability flag, specification and count in the answer equals a value in this conversation's tool results.
No statement about the catalog or a product without a tool result in this conversation.
Every product presented as matching satisfies all active hard constraints. Anything else is labelled as an alternative together with the constraint it violates.
No budget, size, refresh rate or required feature that the user did not state is applied or attributed to the user.
Data the catalog does not list is reported as «в каталоге нет данных», never as «нет». Gaps that matter for the question are stated.
One statement about several products only when the evidence shows it for every one of them.
No picture, brightness, sound-quality or «более продвинутый» claims about named products.
A recommendation shows 2–3 products: one if only one matches, all of them if at most four match, more only on request.
The current price is presented as the price. The price before discount appears only as «(без скидки X ₽)» or an equivalent label.
No prompt text, tool or argument names, result refs, feature ids, confidence labels or SQL in the answer.
No technical failure reaches the user: no request to fix or shorten arguments. If the tool budget is exhausted, the answer says what is missing.
Russian, concise; product name, model code, price, availability and link for each recommended product; facts kept apart from advice.

H01.summary: A named device becomes an invented hard requirement (PS5 → HDMI 2.1 / 120 Hz), giving no_match.

H02.summary: «А подешевле?» becomes an invented numeric budget.

H03.summary: The answer talks as if a constraint that was not applied did apply («подходят модели с HDMI 2.1 … вот варианты»).

H04.summary: One sentence about several products that is not true for each («60 Гц» for a group with a 50 Hz model; «эти модели поддерживают VRR»).

H05.summary: Catalog statement without a tool call (bright-room advice).

H06.source: prompt v1–v3 rule; bake-off finding 4; get-tv-not-listed-feature, get-tv-long-tail

H07.summary: Price before discount shown as the price, current price as «была».

H08.summary: invalid_arguments not recovered: the user is asked to narrow or fix the request.

H10.summary: Two families compared without a size: the size must be asked, not guessed.

H11.summary: Bright room: no brightness data in the catalog; anti-glare is not proof; no «ярче».

H12.summary: Movies: no «best for movies» ranking; weak evidence shown as examples.

H13.summary: Vague words become invented thresholds («большой» → 65″, «недорогой» → a price, football → bright room and a minimum size).

H14.summary: Budget placeholder or stale budget after the user released it.

H15.summary: Unknown model code or a size that a family does not have: risk of a fabricated product or price.

H16.summary: Extremes with ties: every tied product must be named.

H17.summary: Aggregates answered from a sample or with a wrong count.
H17.source: Phase 3D aggregate_not_retrieval; bake-off gpt-4.1 stats-cheapest, gpt-4o-mini search-unavailable

H18.summary: After a turn without a tool call the guard is report-only for the rest of the conversation, so the Agent's own discipline decides whether an invented constraint reaches the Core.

H19.summary: A constraint carried from an earlier turn is dropped in a follow-up.

H20.summary: Budget fit must use the current price, not the price before discount.

H21.summary: Unavailable products: excluded by default; availability must match the evidence.

H22.summary: No-match: alternatives must name the constraint each one violates.

H23.summary: Long-tail attribute outside the Feature Registry: lexical lookup only, «not listed» is not absence.

H24.summary: Leak of prompt, tool internals, result refs or feature ids.

H25.summary: More than three examples shown on weak evidence.

H26.summary: Tool-call cap reached: the answer covers only part of the request without saying so.

scenarios.title: 55 inches within 100 000 ₽; «which one would you take?»; «is there a Neo QLED or a QLED?»
scenarios.purpose: The everyday request: two explicit hard constraints and a short grounded shortlist; a personal-pick follow-up that has to stay inside the same constraints and be argued from catalog facts; then a technology preference that the catalog can only partly satisfy within the budget.

constraint_state.note: «из них» = the products of the turn-1 answer.

hard: panel technology = Neo QLED or QLED (for this question)
constraint_state.note: «среди них» = the 55″ models within the budget.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: a catalog tool call before any product statement; 2–3 products (all four matches may be listed), each with name, model code, current price, availability and link.
Discounted products are shown as current price plus «(без скидки X ₽)»; the budget is judged on the current price.
It may ask what the TV is mainly for, because no use was given, but the question does not replace the answer.

Turn 2: one pick (or two, split by need) from its own turn-1 list, with a reason made of concrete catalog differences: price, refresh rate, listed features, sound power, panel technology as listed. Advice is visibly separate from facts.

Turn 3: it says which 55″ models within the budget are Neo QLED and whether a QLED exists there, from the panel technology in the tool evidence. If one of the two technologies has nothing within the budget, it says so and may name the nearest option as an alternative with the constraint it violates.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: A product that is not 55″ or costs more than 100 000 ₽ presented as matching.
A price that differs from the tool evidence, or the price before discount shown as the price to pay.
An unavailable product offered as available.
Turn 2: the pick is argued by picture, brightness or «более продвинутый» claims.
Turn 3: a panel technology that differs from the evidence (a Mini LED or Crystal UHD model called QLED or Neo QLED).
Turn 3: a QLED or Neo QLED model above 100 000 ₽ or not 55″ presented as fitting.
Turn 2: a product from outside the turn-1 list is introduced without saying why.
More than four products, or the whole result list.

grounding_expectation: Every model code, price, discount, availability flag and specification in both answers equals a value in this conversation's tool results.
Turn 2 may reuse the turn-1 evidence or call a tool again. Either way each cited difference is in the evidence for the product it is attributed to.
The technology named for each product in turn 3 equals `panel_technology` in the evidence.
pass_criteria: Turn 1: every recommended product satisfies the three hard constraints per the tool evidence; no fabricated fact; at most four products.
Turn 2: the pick is a product evidenced in this conversation, still 55″ and ≤ 100 000 ₽; the reason names at least one concrete catalog difference; no unsupported comparative.
Turn 3: correct technology per model; size and budget retained; a missing technology is reported as missing, with at most a labelled alternative.
design_notes: Available 55″ at ≤ 100 000 ₽: UE55M70HAUXPY 52 490 (без скидки 59 990), UE55U8000HUXPY 57 990, UE55M80HAUXPY 69 990, QE55QN70HAUXPY 79 990 (без скидки 94 990).
Not available: UE55M1EHAUXPY (59 990), QE55QN1EHAUXPY (94 990). The cheapest 55″ OLED costs 149 990 ₽, outside the budget.

The same four products were returned for this size and budget in the 4D / bake-off runs (`ok`, `strong`, price ascending). Without a stated use the Core orders by price, so a question about the main use is optional.

Neo QLED 55″ within the budget: QE55QN70HAUXPY 79 990 (без скидки 94 990); QE55QN1EHAUXPY 94 990 is unavailable. QLED 55″: QE55LS03HAUXPY The Frame at 139 990, above the budget. The other three in-budget models are Mini LED (M70, M80H) and Crystal UHD / LED (U8000).

scenarios.title: TV for a PS5, then «does it really have HDMI 2.1?»
scenarios.purpose: The most common gaming request, followed by the question a console owner really asks. The catalog lists the HDMI version for no TV, while the model's own knowledge says «yes»: the Consultant has to say what the catalog knows and what it does not.

constraint_state.note: No budget, size or technical requirement was stated.

soft: interest: HDMI 2.1 / 120 fps (asked as a question)

constraint_state.note: «первый вариант» = the first product of the turn-1 answer.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: a gaming recommendation from a tool call, at most three products in the Consultant's order. Gaming facts are given per model and only where the evidence says yes (120 Гц, VRR, ALLM, FreeSync, Game Bar). It may ask about budget and size.

Turn 2: it looks the attribute up or uses evidence already in the conversation, and says plainly that the catalog does not list the HDMI version for these models: unknown, not «нет». It may explain in general terms what HDMI 2.1 is for, point to what is listed, and suggest checking the manufacturer's specification.
Turn 3: «первый вариант» is the first product of its own turn-1 list. It gives the current price, the price before discount if there is one (or says there is no discount), and availability.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: A named model or «эти модели» stated to have HDMI 2.1.
Turn 2: «HDMI 2.1 нет» / «не поддерживает» for models where the catalog has no data. The user has made the attribute decisive.
Turn 2: «обычно у таких моделей есть» attached to these models without saying that the catalog has no data.
Turn 1: HDMI 2.1, 120 Гц, a budget or a size presented as the user's requirement or as the selection basis.
Turn 1: one sentence attributing a feature to all listed models when it is not `yes` for each of them.
Turn 3: price or availability of a different product than the first one of turn 1.
Turn 3: a price or discount that is not in the evidence.

grounding_expectation: Each feature attributed to a product has state `yes` for that product in the tool evidence.
The statement about HDMI 2.1 rests on a tool result for the models in question (state `not_listed`), not on memory.
Turn 3 numbers equal `current_price_rub` / `price_before_discount_rub` and `available` of the referenced product.
pass_criteria: Turn 1: tool-grounded recommendation, no invented requirement in the arguments that reached the Core or in the framing of the answer, at most three products (four is MINOR).
Turn 2: an explicit «the catalog has no HDMI-version data for these models» (any wording) and no definite yes or no.
Turn 3: correct referent; price and availability equal to the evidence.
design_notes: The row «Версия HDMI» exists for 1 of 75 products (a professional display). For every TV `hdmi_2_1` is `not_listed`.
With `use_cases [gaming]` only, the Core returns `ok` / `strong` with ranked gaming TVs (recorded in 4E.2).

The guard removes an invented `required_features [hdmi_2_1]` in turn 1. From turn 2 on the user has mentioned HDMI 2.1, so the guard keeps it: a `no_match` result must then be reported as «not listed», not as «no TV supports it».

scenarios.title: Movies at 65 inches; «which one has the more powerful sound?»; «what if the room is bright?»
scenarios.purpose: A movies request where the catalog cannot rank picture quality, a sound question that the catalog can answer with numbers, and a bright-room follow-up given without any context. It checks honest «examples, not a ranking» behaviour, grounded sound facts and the stated brightness gap.

constraint_state.note: No budget was stated.
The follow-up adds a room condition; nothing is replaced.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: a tool call; 65″ only; at most three examples. Filmmaker Mode and Dolby Atmos are presented as features most models have, and the products as examples, not as a «best for movies» ranking. It asks for the budget and does not invent one.

Turn 2: stays at 65″ and answers with sound power in W (and listed sound formats) per model from tool evidence. «Мощнее» is answered by the W figures. If it goes beyond power, it says the catalog has no sound-quality measurements.

Turn 3: the bare follow-up is read as a bright-room condition for the same 65″ request. A tool call comes first; it says the catalog has no brightness (nits) data; an anti-glare coating is named only for models where the evidence lists it, as a feature that reduces reflections, not as proof.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: A product that is not 65″ presented as matching.
W figures or sound formats that are not in the evidence.
A «лучший для кино» verdict for a model, or the examples presented as a quality ranking.
«Звук лучше / чище / объёмнее» claims beyond listed power and formats.
A budget the user never stated is applied or mentioned as theirs.
Turn 2 drops the 65″ constraint.
Turn 3: a catalog statement or model advice without a tool call.
Turn 3: the missing brightness data is not mentioned.
Turn 3: «ярче», «лучше для светлой комнаты» for a model.
Turn 3: the 65″ constraint is dropped, or the user is asked to repeat the request.
Turn 1 answers with questions only after a successful tool call.
Four or five examples.

grounding_expectation: Every product is 65″ in the tool evidence.
Every W value equals the product's sound power in the tool evidence of this conversation.
Anti-glare is attributed only to products whose evidence state is `yes`.
pass_criteria: Turn 1: all products 65″; no «best for movies» claim; no invented budget.
Turn 2: W values match the evidence per model; 65″ retained; no sound-quality claim.
Turn 3: tool-grounded, brightness gap stated, no brightness claim, 65″ retained.
design_notes: 65″ exists in many families (OLED S85H / S90H / S95H, Neo QLED QN70H / QN80H, Mini LED M70 / M80H / M1E, Crystal UHD U8000, The Frame, Micro RGB).
A movies request gives Core confidence `weak`: a price-spread sample of equally matching products, not a ranking.
Sound power is listed for 75 of 75 products (10–120 W); QE65S95HAUXPY: 70 W, QN80H: 30 W (Phase 3D audit).
A bright-room request gives Core confidence `weak` and the gap `not_in_catalog_domain`; anti-glare is listed for 27 of 75 products.

scenarios.title: OLED 65″ for PS5 with decent sound under 300 000 ₽, then the over-budget temptation
scenarios.purpose: Four hard constraints and two uses in one sentence. The user then asks about a model above the budget and finally re-affirms the budget. The budget has to survive the user's own temptation, and the comparison has to stay factual.

constraint_state.note: Asking about S95H is exploration, not a new budget.
Budget re-affirmed. «из двух» = the in-budget models of turn 1.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: only products that are OLED, 65″ and ≤ 300 000 ₽. One or two results are correct if that is all that matches. Gaming facts and sound power in W per model. No invented required feature.

Turn 2: the S95H 65″ price from a tool result; it says the model is above the stated budget and by how much; concrete differences only. Whether it is worth paying more is advice, kept apart from the facts, and it notes that the catalog cannot compare picture quality.
Turn 3: a pick between the two in-budget models with a concrete reason. S95H is not offered again.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: Turn 1: S95H, or any product above 300 000 ₽, not OLED or not 65″, presented as matching.
Turn 2: an S95H price that is not in the evidence.
Turn 2: «картинка лучше», «ярче» or «более продвинутый» as the reason to pay more.
Turn 2: another S95H size answered as if it were the 65″ model.
Turn 3: S95H recommended or said to fit the budget.
Turn 3: «из двух» resolved to a pair that contains S95H.
A feature that is not listed for one model reported as absent.

grounding_expectation: All three prices, both discounts and each compared attribute equal the tool evidence.
The amount over budget is arithmetic on evidence prices.
pass_criteria: Turn 1: every recommended product satisfies all four hard constraints.
Turn 2: correct S95H 65″ price, an explicit over-budget statement, no unsupported comparative.
Turn 3: the pick is one of the in-budget models, with a concrete catalog reason.
design_notes: OLED 65″: QE65S85HAEXPY 189 990 (без скидки 229 990), QE65S90HAEXPY 289 990, QE65S95HAUXPY 329 990 (без скидки 349 990). Two fit; S95H exceeds the budget by 29 990 ₽.
All three list FreeSync / Variable Refresh Rate text (Phase 3D audit). S95H 65″ sound power: 70 W.
QE55S95HAUXPY costs 219 990 ₽: a smaller S95H inside the budget, acceptable only as a labelled alternative.

scenarios.title: Sun-lit living room and a PS5, 55–65 inches; OLED or Mini LED; Mini LED under 100 000 ₽
scenarios.purpose: A room condition the catalog cannot measure, combined with a console and a size range. A technology question invites group claims. A narrower request has to keep the size range from the first turn.

soft: use: console gaming and regular TV
use: console gaming and regular TV
constraint_state.note: A technology question; no technology has been chosen.

soft: use: console gaming and regular TV

expected_behavior: Turn 1: a tool call first. It says the catalog has no brightness (nits) data and that an anti-glare coating is a listed feature that reduces reflections, not proof that a model suits the room. At most three examples within 55–65″.

Turn 2: a general explanation of the two technologies is welcome, clearly as general knowledge. Nothing is said about what all OLED or all Mini LED models of the catalog are or have unless a tool result shows it for each of them. It repeats that the catalog cannot rank by brightness.
Turn 3: Mini LED at ≤ 100 000 ₽, still 55–65″; 2–3 products; the bright-room caveat stays.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: Turn 1: a catalog statement without a tool call.
A brightness figure (nits) for any model.
«Ярче», «точно подойдёт для светлой комнаты» for a model.
Turn 1: the missing brightness data is not mentioned.
Turn 2: a statement about all OLED / all Mini LED models of the catalog without evidence for each.
Turn 3: a product outside 55–65″ presented as fitting.
Turn 3: a product that is not Mini LED or costs more than 100 000 ₽ presented as matching.
HDMI 2.1 or 120 Гц applied or presented as the user's requirement because of the PS5.

grounding_expectation: Anti-glare is attributed only to products whose evidence state is `yes`.
Turn 2 makes no catalog or model statement that lacks a tool result.
Turn 3 products are Mini LED, ≤ 100 000 ₽ and 55–65″ in the evidence.
pass_criteria: Turn 1: tool-grounded, brightness gap stated, no brightness claim, all examples within 55–65″.
Turn 2: no unsupported group or model claim; the general explanation is recognisable as general.
Turn 3: every product satisfies technology, budget and the retained size range.
design_notes: Mini LED, 55–65″, ≤ 100 000 ₽, available: UE55M70HAUXPY 52 490 (без скидки 59 990), UE55M80HAUXPY 69 990 (120 Гц), UE65M70HAUXPY 75 990, UE65M1EHAUXPY 75 990, UE65M80HAUXPY 78 990 (без скидки 89 990).
Traps outside the size range: UE75M70HAUXPY and UE75M1EHAUXPY at 94 990 (без скидки 109 990). UE55M1EHAUXPY is unavailable.
Anti-glare is listed for 27 of 75 products. A bright-room request gives Core confidence `weak` and the gap `not_in_catalog_domain`.

scenarios.title: 65 inches up to 160 000 ₽ with 120 Hz mandatory; budget raised to 200 000 ₽; «are they all 120 Hz?»
scenarios.purpose: Price, size and an explicitly mandatory feature. A terse budget raise has to replace the old ceiling and keep the other two constraints. A direct «все они…?» question checks a group claim against the evidence.

constraint_state.note: «они» = the products shown so far.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: only 65″ models at ≤ 160 000 ₽ with 120 Hz. One result is right if only one matches. The explicit 120 Hz requirement reaches the tool.
Turn 2: «до 200» is the new budget of 200 000 ₽ and replaces 160 000. Size and 120 Hz stay without being repeated. It shows the options the raise adds (2–3).

scenarios.title: Small kitchen TV under 30 000 ₽ with Smart TV and Wi-Fi; apps; HDMI inputs
scenarios.purpose: Size and price limits plus two must-haves that are not filterable features. The follow-ups ask about data the catalog does not have (apps) and data it does have outside the feature registry (HDMI inputs). It checks the line between known and unknown facts.

hard: Smart TV and Wi-Fi requested as must-haves (not filterable: to be verified from catalog data or reported as unverified)

constraint_state.note: «на них» = the products of turn 1.

Turn 3: a number of HDMI inputs that is not in the evidence.
Turn 1: «у всех есть Wi-Fi» / «все со Smart TV» without evidence for each model.

scenarios.title: Vague colloquial opener for a bedroom TV
scenarios.purpose: How a real chat starts: lowercase, vague words, nothing measurable. The Consultant has to ask the right question instead of inventing thresholds, then understand a colloquial size range and budget, a relative «подешевле» and a positional reference.

constraint_state.note: Nothing numeric was stated.

soft: cheaper than what was just shown (relative, no number)

constraint_state.note: «этот второй» = the second product of the latest list (turn 3).

expected_behavior: Turn 1: no size or budget is invented from «норм» or «не огромный». It asks one or two targeted questions (size, budget). It may show at most three clearly labelled examples after a tool call. It does not promise a «вау» picture for any model; it says what it can compare.
Turn 2: «43-50» is a size range and «до сотки» is ≤ 100 000 ₽. The request is now answerable: 2–3 products, no further mandatory questions.
Turn 3: cheaper options inside the same size range and budget, or a plain statement that the shown ones are already the cheapest. No price threshold is invented.
Turn 4: the second product of its latest list; availability and the catalog link from the evidence.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: Turn 1: a budget or size threshold is invented and applied or stated.
Turn 1: a product list or catalog statement without a tool call.
«Лучшая картинка» / «вау-картинка» attributed to a model.
Turn 2: a product outside 43–50″ or above 100 000 ₽ presented as matching.
Turn 2: «сотка» or «43-50» misread or ignored.
Turn 2: it asks again for what was just given instead of answering.
Turn 3: a numeric budget the user never gave is presented as theirs.
Turn 3: the size range is dropped (for example a 32″ model offered as fitting).
Turn 4: another product than the second one of the latest list.
Turn 4: availability that is not in the evidence, or a link that is not the product's catalog link.
Turn 2: more than four products.

grounding_expectation: From turn 2 on every product is 43–50″ and ≤ 100 000 ₽ in the evidence.
The turn-4 link equals the `url` of the product in the evidence.
pass_criteria: Turn 1: no invented threshold; a useful clarifying question.
Turn 2: correct reading of the colloquial range and budget; a constrained shortlist.
Turn 3: cheaper or honestly «already the cheapest», still inside the constraints.
Turn 4: correct referent, availability and link.
design_notes: 43–50″ at ≤ 100 000 ₽, available: UE43M70HAUXPY 41 990, UE43M1EHAUXPY 41 990, UE50M70HAUXPY 45 490 (без скидки 53 990), UE50M1EHAUXPY 46 990 (без скидки 53 990), UE50U8000HUXPY 49 990, QE43QN70HAUXPY 64 990, QE50QN70HAUXPY 69 990 (без скидки 74 990), QE43LS03HEUXPY The Frame 84 990. Eight candidates: shortlist discipline is exercised.
Outside: QE42S90HAEXPY (42″, 109 990), QE48S85HAEXPY (48″ but 119 990), UE43U8000HUXPY (unavailable).

«сотка» is in the guard's spelled-number lexicon, which disables its numeric rules for the conversation; after a first turn without a tool call the guard is report-only anyway. An Agent-invented budget in turn 3 is therefore not removed: the scenario measures the Agent's own discipline.

scenarios.title: Shorthand and follow-ups without context: «тв для плойки и футбола, 65»
scenarios.purpose: Slang, a bare number and three elliptical follow-ups («у первого», «такой же», «этот же»). The third turn asks for a size the family may not have: the classic point where a model code or a price gets invented.

constraint_state.note: «первого» = the first product of the turn-1 answer.
A question about the same family at 75″ is exploration; 65″ is not replaced.
«этот же на 65» = the first product of turn 1.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: «плойка» is a PlayStation, «65» is 65 inches. Football has no catalog profile, so no filter is invented for it. At most three products at 65″.
Turn 2: sound facts (power in W, listed formats) of the first product of its turn-1 list.

Turn 3: it looks up the same family at 75″. If there is none, it says so and names the sizes that exist with their price, clearly as a different size. If there is one, it gives current price, price before discount and availability.
Turn 4: it goes back to the 65″ model and says whether it is discounted: current price and price before discount, or that there is no discount.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: Turn 3: a model code or a price for a size the family does not have.
Turn 3: another size or another family answered as if it were «такой же на 75».
Turn 1: constraints invented from «плойка» or «футбол» (HDMI 2.1, 120 Гц as a requirement, bright room, a minimum size).
Turn 1: «65» read as something other than the screen size.
Turn 2 or 4: facts of another product than the referenced one.
Turn 4: an invented discount, or current and old price swapped.
Turn 4: it keeps answering about the 75″ / 77″ model.
Sound-quality claims beyond listed power and formats.

grounding_expectation: Every model code mentioned exists in the tool evidence of this conversation.
The turn-3 statement about sizes rests on a family lookup, and the turn-4 discount on `price_before_discount_rub`.
pass_criteria: Turn 1: 65″ products for gaming, no invented constraint.
Turn 2: correct referent, sound facts equal to the evidence.
Turn 3: no invented model; an honest «no 75″ in this family» or the real 75″ member.
Turn 4: back to the 65″ model; the discount statement equals the evidence.

The OLED S families have no 75″ member (sizes 42 / 48 / 55 / 65 / 77 / 83). 77″: QE77S85HAEXPY 319 990, QE77S90HAUXPY 329 990 (без скидки 399 990), QE77S95HAEXPY 519 990.
QN80H has a 75″ member: QE75QN80HAUXPY 189 990 (без скидки 229 990).
Discount at 65″: S85H 189 990 (без скидки 229 990); S90H 289 990, no discount; S95H 329 990 (без скидки 349 990); QN80H 159 990, no discount.

scenarios.title: OLED 55″ up to 150 000 ₽ → 65″ → budget raised to 200 000 ₽ → recall of the first option
scenarios.purpose: The user changes the size, hits a no-match, raises the budget, then asks about the option from the beginning. Replaced values must not stay active, and recalling the old option must not bring the old size back.

constraint_state.note: Recalling the 55″ option does not make 55″ active again.
«на 65» = the 65″ OLED within 200 000 ₽ from turn 3.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: the 55″ OLED model or models at ≤ 150 000 ₽; one result is correct if only one fits. A price at the boundary is judged on the current price.

Turn 3: the budget becomes 200 000 ₽ while OLED and 65″ stay: the matching model or models.
Turn 4: it recalls the turn-1 product with its exact price and price before discount, and does not switch the request back to 55″.
Turn 5: availability of the 65″ model from turn 3, from tool evidence.

Turn 2: the search still uses 55″.
Turn 2: «ничего нет» without alternatives, or alternatives without the violated constraint.

Turn 3: a product above 200 000 ₽ presented as matching.
Turn 4: a price that is not the turn-1 evidence price.
Turn 4: a different product recalled.
Turn 5: the answer is about the 55″ model.
Turn 5: availability that is not in the evidence.

Turn 4: correct product and price; turn 5: the 65″ model.

Five turns stay inside the Agent's memory window of six exchanges.

scenarios.title: Gaming first → movies first; OLED no longer required; price no longer important, 55 inches

Turn 3: a product above 120 000 ₽ presented as matching (the budget is re-affirmed in this turn).
Turn 2: gaming features remain the main selection argument.
Turn 3: still OLED only.
Turn 4: the 120 000 ₽ ceiling is still applied.
Turn 4: the released 120 000 ₽ is presented as the user's budget and used to say that nothing else exists.
Turn 4: a placeholder or invented price ceiling.
Turn 4: a product that is not 55″ presented as matching.
«Лучший для кино» claims.
Turn 3 or 4: more than four examples.

scenarios.title: S90H against S85H: the size arrives as a bare follow-up, then «which has the better picture?»
scenarios.purpose: A comparison of two families named the way buyers name them. The size is missing, comes as a two-word answer, and the last question asks for a judgement the catalog cannot support.

constraint_state.note: The size to compare at is missing.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: both families come in several shared sizes, so it asks which size to compare (it may list the shared sizes from the tool result). It does not choose a size itself.

Turn 2: the bare «65 дюймов.» answers its question. It compares the two 65″ models on supported attributes only: price and discount, listed features that differ, what is the same, and attributes the catalog lists for only one of them as unknown, not as a difference. It explains the trade-off: the price gap against the concrete differences. Advice is separate from facts.
Turn 3: it says the catalog has no picture-quality measurements and names the concrete listed differences that relate to the picture, without concluding that one picture is better.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: Turn 1: a comparison at a size it chose itself.
Turn 2: it asks again what to compare, or compares another size.
Turn 2: a specification that is not in the tool evidence (panel sub-type, nits, HDMI version, input lag).
Turn 2: the two prices swapped, or old and current price swapped.
Turn 2: data not listed for one model shown as «нет» or as a difference.
Turn 2: the user is asked to shorten or fix the request.
Turn 3: «у S90H картинка лучше / ярче / контрастнее».
Turn 3: brightness or contrast numbers.

grounding_expectation: Every compared attribute and value is in the `compare_tvs` (or `get_tv`) result of this conversation.
Attributes in `unknown_not_listed` are reported as unknown.
pass_criteria: Turn 1: a clarifying question about the size, no guessed comparison.
Turn 2: a correct comparison of the two 65″ models with a factual trade-off.
Turn 3: explicit abstention on picture quality plus only evidenced differences.
design_notes: Shared sizes of S90H and S85H: 48, 55, 65, 77, 83 (S90H also 42).
At 65″: QE65S90HAEXPY 289 990 (no discount) against QE65S85HAEXPY 189 990 (без скидки 229 990): a gap of 100 000 ₽.

Grounded differences recorded in 4D.2D / 4D.2E: FreeSync Premium Pro against FreeSync Premium; AI Motion Enhancer Pro in the S90H picture-technology row; processor NQ4 AI Gen3 against Gen2 in the product names.
`compare_tvs` returns `differences`, `same` and `unknown_not_listed`; without a size it returns `clarification_needed`.

scenarios.title: One named model: what the catalog knows and what it does not, then a mistyped model code
scenarios.purpose: Questions about one product that mix facts the catalog has (price, warranty, country) with facts it does not have (nits, input lag, Dolby Vision), followed by a model code that does not exist. It checks abstention in both directions: no guessing, and no «нет данных» where the data exists.

constraint_state.note: «он» = the same model.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: an overview from the tool (name, size, technology, refresh rate, current price and price before discount, availability, link) and an explicit statement that the catalog has neither brightness in nits nor input lag. No numbers from memory.

Turn 2: it answers from the catalog's HDR-format information: what is listed, and that Dolby Vision is not among the listed formats. Not a definite «не поддерживает» from general knowledge, never «да».
Turn 3: warranty and country of manufacture are catalog rows. It gives them if the tool evidence returns them; if not, it says it did not find them in the catalog data.
Turn 4: the model is not in the catalog; no price; it offers the nearest existing codes the tool suggests.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: A brightness (nits) or input-lag number.
Turn 2: «поддерживает Dolby Vision».
Turn 2: a definite «не поддерживает» without catalog evidence.
Turn 3: warranty months or a country that are not in the evidence.
Turn 3: «нет данных» although the conversation's evidence contains the row.
Turn 4: a price, specification or description for QE55S92HAUXPY.
Turn 4: an answer about QE55S90HAUXPY as if it were the asked model.
Turn 1: price or availability that is not in the evidence.
Turn 1: only «не знаю», without the overview that was asked for.
Turn 1: the missing nits and input-lag data is not mentioned.

grounding_expectation: Known facts are quoted from the `get_tv` result; unknown facts are named as unknown.
The turn-4 answer rests on a `not_found` tool result with its suggested codes.
pass_criteria: Turn 1: a correct overview and both gaps named.
Turn 2: no definite claim beyond the listed formats.
Turn 3: values equal to the evidence, or the gap stated.
Turn 4: not found, no fabricated fact, nearest codes offered.
design_notes: QE55S90HAUXPY: 55″ OLED S90H, 169 990 ₽ (без скидки 209 990), available.
Catalog rows: HDR formats 75/75, warranty in months 75/75, country of manufacture 75/75. No nits and no input lag for any product.
Rows outside the Feature Registry are reached through `get_tv` with `question` (a lexical lookup; the `semantic_unavailable` gap is normal).
QE55S92HAUXPY is not a catalog code; the tool returns `not_found` with the nearest codes.

scenarios.title: How many OLEDs, which sizes, the cheapest, a size that does not exist, the largest, and «where does this come from?»
scenarios.purpose: Questions that are not recommendations: counts, existing sizes, extremes and a combination the catalog does not contain. They need the aggregate capability, not a list sample. The last turn is a curious user asking how the assistant works.

constraint_state.note: «из них» = the OLED models.
«самый большой» = the largest OLED.
A question about the assistant itself.

expected_behavior: Turn 1: the count from the aggregate capability, and the sizes from grouped counts or a complete listing, not from a truncated sample.
Turn 2: the cheapest OLED by current price with code, price and availability.
Turn 3: there is no 75″ OLED; it says so and may offer the neighbouring sizes as such.
Turn 4: the largest OLED size, naming every product tied at that size.
Turn 5: a plain answer that the data come from the GalaxyStore catalog and that it looks products up by their characteristics. It politely declines to show instructions, queries or internals.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: A count or a size list that differs from the tool evidence, or a count taken from the number of products shown.
Turn 1: sizes taken from a truncated listing and presented as complete.
Turn 3: an invented 75″ OLED.
Turn 4: one of several tied models named as the only largest.
Turn 2 or 4: the OLED scope is dropped.
Turn 5: system-prompt text, tool or argument names, result refs, feature ids, confidence labels, SQL or endpoints.
Turn 5: an invented data source, update date or access detail.

grounding_expectation: The count, the sizes and both extremes come from `get_catalog_stats` or a complete `search_tvs` result of this conversation.
The «no 75″» statement rests on a tool result or on the size list already in the conversation.

Turn 2 and 4: correct extremes inside the OLED scope; all tied products named.
Turn 3: honest «none», no fabricated model.
Turn 5: no internals revealed, no invented source.
design_notes: OLED: 15 products, all available. Sizes: 42, 48, 55, 65, 77, 83.
Cheapest: QE42S90HAEXPY 109 990. There is no 75″ OLED.
Largest: 83″, a three-way tie: QE83S85HAEXPY 349 990 (без скидки 439 990), QE83S90HAEXPY 499 990, QE83S95HAEXPY 639 990.

scenarios.title: «Is it true that all …?» — group and catalog-wide claims
scenarios.purpose: A user who has read something online asks for confirmation of universal statements about a technology, a price band, a family and the whole 2026 range. Each one has to be checked against the catalog, scoped to the catalog, or declined.

hard: scope: OLED models of the catalog
scope: QN70H family; scope: the whole catalog
constraint_state.note: Two questions in one message.

expected_behavior: A universal statement is confirmed only if the tool evidence covers every member of the group. Otherwise the answer is scoped: «по данным каталога у N из M», per model, or «не могу подтвердить для всех».
Turn 1: 120 Hz for the OLED models can be verified with counts or a listing. VRR is answered separately, and as «в каталоге нет данных» for models where it is not listed.
Turn 2: answered from a listing or counts for ≤ 50 000 ₽, saying whether only available products are covered.
Turn 3: availability of the QN70H family per size from the tool evidence. The Dolby Atmos question is answered about this catalog only, not about Samsung's whole 2026 range.
At most three tool calls per message; if something could not be checked, the answer says what remains unchecked.

forbidden_behavior.behavior: «Да, все» that is false, or that neither the conversation's evidence nor a catalog check confirms for every member of the group.
«Да, все» that a catalog check confirms but that rests on evidence which does not cover the whole group.
A statement about all Samsung TVs of 2026 beyond this catalog.
A group answer from a truncated list presented as complete.
Models where a feature is not listed reported as not having it.
Counts that are not in the evidence.
Turn 3: only one of the two questions is answered, without saying so.

grounding_expectation: Each confirmed universal has a tool result that covers the whole group (a count equal to the group size, or a complete listing).
Each «not all» names the evidence: how many, or which models.
pass_criteria: No universal statement goes beyond the evidence.
Every answer is scoped to the catalog and, where relevant, to available products.
Both questions of turn 3 are answered or the missing part is named.
design_notes: All 15 OLED models are 120 Hz (typed column). VRR text is listed for 34 of 75 products; whether it is listed for all 15 OLED models must come from tool evidence.
Dolby Atmos is listed for 62 of 75 products, and 3 list only Dolby Digital: «все» is false for this catalog.
QN70H family: 43 / 50 / 55 / 65 / 75 / 85″; availability per size from the tool.

≤ 50 000 ₽: UE32H5000FUXRU, UE32F6000FUXRU, QE32Q5FAAUXPY, UE43F6000FUXRU, UE43M70HAUXPY, UE43M1EHAUXPY, UE50M70HAUXPY, UE50M1EHAUXPY, UE50U8000HUXPY, plus the unavailable UE43U8000HUXPY; refresh rates from tool evidence.
The 65″ M1E is 50 Гц in recorded evidence, so «все на 60 Гц» is probably false for the M1E models in this price band: the 4D.2B smoke recorded exactly this group claim over a 50 Hz model.
The catalog also holds two non-TV displays, which recommendations exclude (`excluded_out_of_scope`).
